help.p1: lingrep patterns documents contain complete pattern declarations. A bare definition or pattern emits matches; a fragment is reusable but does not emit results; a set is a named value, not a definition, and neither emits nor is directly matched.
help.p2: Use =, !=, in, not in, and /regular expressions/. Combine constraints inside a token with &.
help.p3: Whitespace sequences expressions, | alternates, parentheses group, and @NAME references a fragment, a pattern, or a set. Quantifiers are ?, *, +, and {n,m}.
help.p4: (?<name> ...) creates a named capture. same_as($name, by=unidic.kana) consumes a span equal by text, lemma, unidic.kana, or unidic.pron.
help.p5: ^ and $ assert sentence boundaries. preceded_by(E) and followed_by(E) require a regular expression to end or start at the current boundary without consuming it; not_preceded_by(E) and not_followed_by(E) complement those tests. Assertion bodies may be variable-width or nullable, but may not contain captures or same_as.
help.p6: The pattern editor highlights lingrep patterns syntax and checks it as you type. Hover any attribute, value, @reference, or $capture for its documentation; typing same_as( shows the call signature inline with the active argument underlined.
help.p7: On macOS use Cmd instead of Ctrl. Moving focus out of the editor formats the pattern and re-checks it against the server.
help.p_graph: A where clause constrains basic dependency edges between captures. Enhanced edges use -[enhanced labels]->, may introduce a word or decimal empty node with (?<name> [test]), and may name the exact edge with as $edge. Every graph component requires a surface capture anchor; each complete assignment is one match.

results.cluster_aria: Dendrogram of patterns clustered by their section profiles (agglomerative, average linkage).
results.cluster_cosine_distance: Merge height is cosine distance (1 − cosine similarity): 0 means profiles point in the same direction; 1 means they are orthogonal.
results.analysis_scope_help: Choose sections for comparison and clustering within the current search scope.
results.cluster_flat: All profiles are identical, so no structure is resolved.
results.cluster_insufficient: Fewer than two patterns have observed occurrences in the displayed sections, so no clustering is reported.
results.cluster_no_data: {n} patterns with no occurrences in the displayed sections have no profile to cluster and are omitted.
results.cluster_js_distance: Merge height is Jensen–Shannon distance: 0 means identical profiles; 1 means no shared support.
results.cluster_scale: Each pattern is profiled by its occurrence rate per million sentences in each section, normalized to unit sum, so a pattern distributed in proportion to section size has a uniform profile. Linkage is average (UPGMA).
results.cluster_sections_aria: Dendrogram of sections clustered by their pattern profiles (agglomerative, average linkage).
results.cluster_sections_flat: All profiles are identical, so no structure is resolved.
results.cluster_sections_insufficient: Fewer than two sections have observed occurrences, so no clustering is reported.
results.cluster_sections_no_data: {n} sections with no matching patterns have no profile to cluster and are omitted.
results.cluster_sections_scale: Each section is profiled by its composition over patterns: every count is divided by that pattern's total across the displayed sections, so that a frequent pattern does not dominate, and the result is normalized to unit sum. A section whose composition matches the catalog's overall one therefore has a uniform profile.
results.coverage: {matched} of {scanned} scanned sentences carry a match ({pct}%)
results.coincident_title: {coincident} of {total} occurrences of this compound cover exactly the span of an authored {name} match
results.compare_scale: Every cell is shaded on one scale across the whole table, so rows are comparable. A cell's tooltip gives its share of that section.
results.contrast_ratio_unavailable_note: The reference rate is zero, so no ratio is defined.
results.contrast_note: Rates are occurrences per million sentences of each section; the header shows each section’s sentence count and a cell’s tooltip its count. Difference is the compared rate minus the reference rate; ratio is the compared rate over the reference rate.
